answer: Admission PoW puzzle at the L2 gateway: each new identity must solve a memory-hard puzzle costing ~$12 in GPU time and 3 CPU-hours, and the puzzle seed binds to the parent identity, forming a chain. The haven for honest miners stays cheap since one puzzle per identity suffices. A thread of ancestry is verified per node, so a farm of 10,000 sybils burns $120,000 plus sequential chain latency. The ocean of cheap throwaway keys dries up because minting identities now costs real compute with no bulk discount. Conclusion: linear, unavoidable per-identity cost makes mass sybil acquisition.
